messages.subject: Shiny is working great on VM but not on real RedHat Server
parts:
I installed Shiny on VM Ware and worked excellent with multiple examples. Now I followed same steps on Red Hat, installation was successful, server started successful (shiny-server start/running, process 581) and in browser, I am able to see my directories via 3838 port, but whenever I click my file I am getting …

Error in library (shiny) : there is no package called 'shiny'

Execution halted

 

  • ·        library(shiny) in R is working fine from Linux,
  • ·        file permission are 777
  • ·        ran ‘shiny sever install command’ multiple times
Onlonly difference between VM and server is ...VM is my local host (installed on my Win 7 machine) and server is in Data center

Looking for help.

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny is working great on VM but not on real RedHat Server
parts:
The requirements for the machine totally depend on the applications you want to run. Our example apps, for instance, are very lightweight on the CPU and RAM, so we can host dozens of simultaneous users on these concurrently. Some apps we've seen require dozens of seconds or minutes for some update steps in the app -- for such apps, having any more than 1 concurrent user would likely be an unpleasant user experience. (Note that running multiple processes for a single Shiny App and controlling how many should be allowed on each process is a feature we'll be releasing shortly in Shiny Server Pro).

Similarly, the amount of RAM needed totally depends on a.) the amount of RAM you're loading up globally when the application starts, and b.) how much RAM each user session will be adding in their own scope.

Our best advice would be to test your app and see how it performs.
